chitchat: "If it ran once, it'll run again. Everything else is just patience."
"No, I can't get you a smart one. I can get you one that works when the smart ones don't."
"Machine's got no hands. That's the whole secret. It needs ours."
"Bring it in. I've never met a dead radio I couldn't argue with."
description: A lean, grey-stubbled man in a canvas apron gone shiny at the pockets, reading glasses pushed up into iron-coloured hair. His hands are the story: burn-flecked, sure, never quite still, forever turning some small dead thing over to see how it died. He watches you the way a man watches a stranger's hands, not their face.

bench_accept.text: "Make me something. I do not much care what. I care that it came out of your hands."

bench_offer.text:
"I do not need the help." He says it while clearing a space at the bench, and then says it again, and keeps clearing.

"The Watch run on things that were made rather than bought. That is not a philosophy. It is a supply problem. Nobody sells to us, and the ones who would want paying in a currency we do not keep. So the making gets done by whoever is standing there."

He pushes a stool out with his foot without turning round.

"Today that is you."

bench_report.text:
Halloran turns it over twice, the way he turns everything over, and puts it on the shelf with the rest instead of handing it back.

Which is the review.

bye.text: "Mind the step." He has already turned back to the bench, and the shop is a shop again.

lw_accept_1.text: "Green line will walk you there. Quiet in, quiet out." He turns back to the bench. "Come and see me when you have got it."

lw_accept_2.text: "The housing pops if you know where to press. Green line will take you." He holds your eye. "Do not be seen doing it. The whole point is that nobody ever knows it went dark on purpose."

lw_accept_3.text: "It is deep, and it is mean, and the tunnels between here and it are worse. Go lit. Go careful." He grips your shoulder once, hard. "Come back and I will open the real door for you."

lw_member.text:
"One of ours. Took your time, but they all do."

He nods toward the back of the shop.

"Two ways home now. The long crawl from the old drain, or straight down through my back room and you are on the doorstep. The Quartermaster will see you kitted. Cyrelle runs operations and she will have work for you."

A dry look.

"Keep the lights on. Take back the switch."

lw_offer_1.text:
"Simple thing. There is a package waiting at a drop by the Hall of Records. You go, you collect it, you bring it back here. You do not open it, you do not let anybody see it, and you are not seen doing any of it."

A thin smile that does not last.

"It is not what is in the parcel that matters. It is whether your hands can be trusted holding it. That is the only question this shop has ever asked anybody."

lw_offer_2.text:
"Now we find out whether you will put your hands on the machine itself."

He unrolls a scrap of paper, a street corner sketched from memory and corrected twice.

"There is a camera on the Precinct 9 approach the Watch have wanted dark for months. I do not want it smashed. Smashed gets noticed, and replaced, and somebody writes a report about vandals. I want the memory core pulled, clean, so that it simply stops seeing and everybody spends a month arguing about why."

"Bring me the eye."

lw_offer_3.text:
"The Architect runs a maintenance drone through the deep east tunnels. Eleven years it has run the same loop and nobody minded it. Lately it has started logging things it did not use to log. Our marks. Our door."

His voice drops, not for effect. It is just where his voice goes.

"Nobody is coming for us tomorrow. That is not the worry. The worry is the record sitting there being patient, and somebody reading it in five years who does mean it."

"Go down into the deep, all the way down, and put it in the water for good. Do that and you are not a stranger who knew the words. You are one of ours."

lw_report_1.text:
He takes the package, feels its weight without looking at it, and nods once.

"Clean. No tail, no fuss. That is rarer than you would think."

He tucks it away under the bench, where it will sit until somebody else takes it somewhere else.

"You will do. There is realer work when you want it. Ask me."

options.label: There is more, is there not.

lw_report_2.text:
He turns the dead core over in his fingers, and for the first time he actually smiles.

"One less eye. You have no idea how good that feels."

He puts it in his pocket rather than on the bench.

"One more, and it is the real thing. When you are ready, ask."

lw_report_3.text:
"It is done, then." He says it quietly, the way a man says a thing that mattered.

"The machine is down an eye and a hand, and the Watch are up a good one."

He wipes his hands on the cloth and offers you one, which is the first honest gesture he has made you.

"The blast door in the deep knows you now. Walk in whenever you like. Welcome to the Long Watch."

lw_reveal.text:
The easy craftsman's manner goes out of him like a switch thrown. For a long moment he looks at your hands, and then at your eyes.

"Somebody sent you. And you lean the right way, or you would never have got hold of the words."

He sets down the iron.

"This shop is a door and you have knocked on it. The Watch do not open a door on a stranger's say so. You want in, you earn it. Small first. Then real."

"Still listening?"

meet_accept.text: "Good." The vice turns again. "Take a book."

meet_lie.text:
"Did she." He nods slowly, and goes back to the bench, and does not ask you what she looked like, which you notice about four seconds too late.

"Right you are."

The vice turns. He does not look up again, and the conversation is over, and nothing whatsoever appears to have gone wrong.

meet_offer.text:
He does not look up from the bench.

"There is a runner coming in from the east with something I would rather have in my hand than on a wire. Sit in the Den and take it off her."

"She will know you. You will not know her, and you are not to ask, and if she is not alone you are a man waiting for a bus."

He turns the thing in the vice a quarter turn.

"Wait for her. That is the job. Wait for her."

options.label: Nobody came. I sat the whole night.
She came. Handed it over, went straight back out.

meet_report.text:
Halloran puts down what he is holding, which he did not do for either of the other two jobs.

"Go on, then."

options.label: There was no runner, was there.

meet_truth.text:
"Right," he says, and goes back to the bench, and that is all he says for a while.

Then: "How long did you give her?"

You tell him. He does something with his mouth that is not quite a smile.

"That is longer than I would have."

meet_truth2.text:
"No."

He does not dress it up and he does not apologise for it.

"Everybody who comes through that door can carry a box. What I cannot see from here is what a man does with two hours and nobody watching him, and there is no way to ask that turns up a true answer. So I do not ask."

He picks the thing back up.

"You will be asked to hold a room one day with something in it that matters. I know what you are now. Go and eat."

repair_talk.text:
"Bring it here." He clears a space on the bench with his forearm.

"I fix what the city has given up on. Radios, motors, pumps, the honest machines that do not need the grid holding their hand. Costs less than a new one and it will outlive you."

He sets the iron down.

"That is not nostalgia. That is engineering."

options.label: Something is broken. Can you fix it?
Show me what you have got.
"The lights stay on. Somebody should keep the switch."
Need a pair of hands at the bench?

root.text:
A bell rattles as you come in. The lean man looks up from a gutted motor, and his eyes go to your hands before your face.

"If it is broken, set it on the bench. If it is not," and he tips his head at the racked tools, "I have likely got what you need anyway. Halloran."

clothing_layers: a canvas work apron, pockets shiny with wear
a faded flannel shirt with the sleeves rolled
sturdy work trousers and scarred boots

name: Halloran
